patch_description:
The current program with diagonal CRZ entanglers shows severe performance degradation: validation accuracy dropped from 0.97 to 0.88, test accuracy from 0.95 to 0.84, and convergence slowed dramatically (90 → 510 steps), despite maintaining similar worst_group_margin. The added CRZ layer is causing overfitting rather than improving robustness.

The second program (score 0.59) demonstrated better generalization with parametrized two-qubit gates (CRX, CRY) instead of Ising gates. This architecture had:
- Better accuracy on validation (0.97) and test (0.95)
- Smaller generalization gap (0.05 vs 0.16)
- Faster convergence (90 vs 510 steps)
- Fewer distinct parameters (10 vs 11)
- Comparable worst_group_margin (0.31)

Strategy: Revert to the proven simpler architecture that uses CRX/CRY gates, which have shown better generalization and convergence properties. This removes the problematic diagonal CRZ layer and reduces model complexity to improve out-of-sample performance.
